headline: Fixed review r1. F1.1 (major): the dtx_gate readout now prints the arm's realised gating dose next to the held-out vad_gate's dose and applies a pre-registered dose rule, so an under-dosed null arm reads 'inconclusive (under-dosed)' instead of 'refuted' / Drop. F1.2: the apm selftest no longer wakes OpenBLAS (its CPU time went from 546.91 s to 0.56 s in checks). F1.3: the first lever failure in each process is now printed in a line the wave's early check catches. checks cpu passes 126/126.

files.purpose: F1.1. Adds DTX_BINS (the same bin edges as dsp_dtx.gated_bin) and heldout_vad_dose() (read from heldout_v1/meta.csv). Adds arm_dtx_dose(): sums the metrics.jsonl b4.aug_by_class dtx_g* counts per class over epochs. Adds the dose rule (dose_ratio < 0.25 means under-dosed; no telemetry means dose unknown). In the dtx_gate lever verdict, the refuted case now reads 'inconclusive (under-dosed / dose unknown)' unless the dose is adequate. Adds dtx_gate_reading with the plan 2.2 falsifiers (1)-(3): falsifier (1) leads to Drop only at an adequate dose, otherwise 'owner decides a dose variant'. Adds the dose and decision print blocks and the JSON keys dtx_dose and dtx_gate_reading.
F1.2: _lag now uses sums of elementwise products instead of np.dot (no OpenBLAS threads). The [aligned] assert is unchanged.

F1.3: new RTCAugmenterB4._lever_failed. It counts every failure and prints the first one per process and op as '[b4wave] <op> failed (<Exc>: ..); <action>'. Used by apm_ns, dtx_gate and opus_plc (on its ffmpeg fallback). New attribute fail_printed. Nothing changes on the levers-off path, which still returns the B3 object.

dsp_slices gains 6 checks: held-out dose reproduces the review; arm dose read from a fabricated metrics.jsonl; bins match the lever; dose rule; lever verdict under the dose rule; falsifier decisions. New group lever_failures (3 checks with raising stubs). CPU_GROUPS and the docstring are updated.

dtx_gate: a 'Dose' bullet, listed as an open issue for the owner, plus the readout bullet (dose, VAD-by-fill, decision lines). Verdict rules gain a 'dtx_gate dose rule' paragraph. Also a note on the apm _lag change, the failure-line telemetry, and the checks rows for lever_failures and dsp_slices.
fix_f1 section: what changed, measurements, decisions; Left updated
full output of checks cpu (126/126 PASS)
F1.2 probe: measure() CPU vs wall time, and the cost of the wrtc_ns calls right after it
F1.1 probe: builds a fabricated dtx_gate arm dir (B2f readouts plus a metrics.jsonl with b4 rows) for the readout

levers.deviations: Readout only (review F1.1), no training change. When the dose cannot be read (no b4 rows), it is treated like under-dosed: no 'refuted'. Falsifier (1)'s plan clause 'with WF1 Δ < +0.5' is read on both readouts: the arm escapes only with WF1 Δ ≥ +0.5 on merge_top5 AND final, following O3.2's both-readouts rule. Falsifiers (2) and (3) are evaluated first and lead to Drop at any dose.
None. The selftest lag search no longer uses BLAS (F1.2), and a failure now prints its first occurrence (F1.3).

The F1.3 failure line is extended to opus_plc's in-process failure ('ffmpeg fallback with the same profile'), which the review did not name. Without it, a systematic libopus failure would silently turn the arm into a B2f replicate.

cpu_results.summary: 126/126 PASS in 272 s (was 117 checks; +6 dsp_slices dose checks, +3 lever_failures). No APM_BALANCE or DTX_BALANCE WARN. Timing factors: apm 1.013, dtx 1.006, opus 0.847. apm selftest CPU 0.56 s (static log had 546.91 s). Log: rdloop/B4/impl/checks_cpu_fix_f1.log
3/3 PASS. apm, dtx and opus each print exactly one '[b4wave] <op> failed (RuntimeError: ...)' line per process; counts 7 / 7 / 24

open_issues: Owner decision before smoke (F1.1 item 3): dtx_gate, as approved, gates far less than the held-out vad_gate. ≥20 %-gated clips are 0.5-2.5 % of training clips (checks dtx_balance) vs 32.1 % on held-out (n 629). The cause is webrtcvad's own 100-330 ms overhang plus the drawn 40-200 ms hangover. The arm trains as planned, and the readout now reports 'inconclusive (under-dosed)' rather than 'refuted' when dose_ratio < 0.25. A higher-dose variant (e.g. hangover U(0, 200) ms, or a higher p) is a training change and needs the owner.
The dose rule's 0.25 threshold and the 'dose unknown ⇒ no refuted' reading are the reviewer's proposed values, implemented as given. The supervisor's re-review should confirm them.
The fork / 64-worker path of the failure print (pid-keyed) is covered by a simulated pid change only. The smoke run is the real test.
progress_note: fix_f1 is done. F1.1: dose readout, dose rule and the dtx falsifier decision lines in scripts/b4_dsp_slices.py, plus README text and 6 checks. F1.2: _lag no longer uses BLAS. F1.3: the first failure per process is printed, with a new lever_failures group. checks cpu passes 126/126; the manifest check finds 0 violations. Left: the supervisor's re-review, GPU checks and smoke. The owner should look at the dtx_gate dose (README 'Dose') before smoke. Details are in rdloop/B4/impl/progress.md under 'fix_f1'.
